tools.name: usage
tools.description: Plan caps for this workspace: plan, period, probe_count, monthly_probe_quota, endpoints_used, max_endpoints, max_regions, min_interval_seconds, sample_retention_days, max_status_pages. Call this before creating anything. Stop when a cap is reached.

tools.name: list_regions
tools.description: Enabled probe regions: id, name, and region.

tools.name: list_checks
tools.description: Checks in this workspace. Use this before create_check so you do not add a second check for a URL that is already watched.

tools.name: get_check
tools.description: One check, including assertion, DNS, and TCP fields. Secrets such as request headers, request body, and HTTP auth are not returned.

tools.name: get_check_results
tools.description: Check results. view is status, history, or outages. history uses hours (default 24) and returns status, status_code, latency_ms, dns_ms, connect_ms, location_name, location_region, and observed_at. Sample metadata is omitted.

tools.name: create_check
tools.description: Create a check. kind is http, api, dns, or tcp. Defaults: GET, status 200, 10s timeout, email alerts on, interval_seconds from the plan minimum, and one region. DNS defaults to an A record over UDP. TCP requires port. Pass regions only when you want more than the default, and only within max_regions

tools.name: update_check
tools.description: Update a check. Pass only the fields to change. enabled false pauses and true resumes. Linking requires site_id, site_slug, and component_id together, plus optional incident_mode (off, auto, or review: review stores a draft a person approves before it is published), incident_auto_resolve, and displa

tools.name: delete_check
tools.description: Delete a check. Run only when the user asked to delete this check in this conversation.

tools.name: run_check
tools.description: Queue a probe for one check. Returns job_id. Call get_check_results with view status for the result; it is not included here.

tools.name: list_status_pages
tools.description: Status pages in this workspace: slug, name, visibility, publicUrl, custom domain, and the worst open incident status.

tools.name: get_status_page
tools.description: One status page: components with ids, groups, incidents with public ids, Slack connection state, and alert-destination ids. has_password is returned; the password is not.

tools.name: create_status_page
tools.description: Create a public status page. visibility internal requires Pro and a password of at least 8 characters that the user typed; never invent a password or repeat it. custom_domain is a hostname such as status.acme.com and requires Pro. With endpoint_ids, each check becomes a component linked to the page

tools.name: update_status_page
tools.description: Update a status page. Fields: name, url, visibility, password, custom_domain, show_auto_detected (label incidents a check opened itself as detected automatically). custom_domain null removes it. visibility internal needs a password of at least 8 characters that the user typed. Never invent a passwor

tools.name: delete_status_page
tools.description: Delete a status page and its components. Run only when the user asked to delete this page in this conversation.

tools.name: verify_custom_domain
tools.description: Check the CNAME and TXT records for a status page custom domain.

tools.name: create_component
tools.description: Add a component to an existing status page. Returns its id so update_check can link a check to it.

tools.name: update_component
tools.description: Rename a component or change its URL.

tools.name: delete_component
tools.description: Delete a component. Run only when the user asked to delete this component in this conversation.

tools.name: manage_component_group
tools.description: Create, update, or delete a component group. action is create, update, or delete. create and update need name. update and delete need group_id. Delete only when the user asked.

tools.name: slack_connection
tools.description: Slack connection for a status page. action start returns a URL for the user to open; do not complete OAuth. action disconnect removes the connection. Disconnect only when the user asked. Connection state is on get_status_page.

tools.name: page_alert_destinations
tools.description: Replace the alert destinations attached to a status page with these existing destination ids. Use list_alert_destinations for the ids. An empty list detaches all of them.

tools.name: list_incident_proposals
tools.description: Drafts waiting for review from checks in incident_mode review, pending first. Approving one publishes it as a status incident.

tools.name: approve_incident_proposal
tools.description: Publish a pending review draft as a status incident. This emails subscribers and posts to Slack. Run only when the user asked to publish it in this conversation. Optional title, body, and impact (minor, major, or critical) replace the draft text.

tools.name: dismiss_incident_proposal
tools.description: Dismiss a pending review draft. Nothing is published.

tools.name: create_incident
tools.description: Open an incident. This emails subscribers and posts to Slack the same way the console does. Run only when the user asked to publish this incident in this conversation. status is investigating, identified, monitoring, or resolved. impact is minor, major, or critical. component_ids are component publi

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident, including updates newest first.

tools.name: update_incident
tools.description: Edit an incident. This can email subscribers and post to Slack. Run only when the user asked. With update_id, edit that posted update instead of the incident. Never invent a status the user did not ask for.

tools.name: post_incident_update
tools.description: Post an incident update. This emails subscribers and posts to Slack. Run only when the user asked to publish this update in this conversation. status resolved closes the incident.

tools.name: list_maintenance_windows
tools.description: Maintenance windows: id, name, starts_at, duration_seconds, timezone, recurrence, weekdays, ends_at, notify_subscribers, and items.

tools.name: create_maintenance_window
tools.description: Schedule a maintenance window. duration_seconds is 60 through 7 days. Pass both the check (endpoint_ids) and its public component (status_components) so probes pause and the page shows Under maintenance. notify_subscribers defaults to false. Set it true only when the user asked to email subscribers.

tools.name: update_maintenance_window
tools.description: Update a maintenance window. notify_subscribers defaults to false unless you set it. This can email subscribers. Run only when the user asked to change this window.

tools.name: cancel_maintenance_window
tools.description: Cancel a maintenance window. notify_subscribers defaults to false. This can email subscribers. Run only when the user asked to cancel this window in this conversation.

tools.name: list_alert_destinations
tools.description: Existing alert destinations: id, kind, name, and hint. Secrets are not returned. Creating a destination stays in the console.

tools.name: test_alert_destination
tools.description: Send a real test alert to an existing destination. Run only when the user asked to send the test.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_checks, create_check, update_check, update_status_page, slack_connection, list_incident_proposals, create_incident, create_maintenance_window · Private data: get_check, create_check, get_status_page, create_status_page, update_status_page, verify_custom_domain, list_alert_destinations · Public sink: create_check, approve_incident_proposal, create_incident, update_incident, post_incident_update, create_maintenance_window, update_maintenance_window, cancel_maintenance_window, test_alert_destination · Destructive: delete_check, run_check, delete_status_page, delete_component, manage_component_group, approve_incident_proposal, create_incident, update_incident, post_incident_update, create_maintenance_window, update_maintenance_window, cancel_maintenance_window, test_alert_destination.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_checks, create_check, update_check, update_status_page, slack_connection, list_incident_proposals, create_incident, create_maintenance_window · Private data: get_check, create_check, get_status_page, create_status_page, update_status_page, verify_custom_domain, list_alert_destinations · Public sink: create_check, approve_incident_proposal, create_incident, update_incident, post_incident_update, create_maintenance_window, update_maintenance_window, cancel_maintenance_window, test_alert_destination · Destructive: delete_check, run_check, delete_status_page, delete_component, manage_component_group, approve_incident_proposal, create_incident, update_incident, post_incident_update, create_maintenance_window, update_maintenance_window, cancel_maintenance_window, test_alert_destination

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
